about: How the ChatGPT/Codex package differs from the repo skills. The /chatgpt endpoint serves only the tools in chatgpt-tools.json: no Blender or Adobe bridges, no social publishing, no ask_mira, no 3D, no raw uploads (chat attachments arrive through the client), no guide publishing, no voice deletion. Every `find` must match the source exactly once, so the build fails as soon as a source edit makes a rewrite stale. `override` files replace a source file whole; `sha256` is the source they were written against, and check.mjs fails when the source moves on without them.

## Publishing

Guides are published by the user in the guide editor on the website, never from here. When a draft
or an edit is ready, give them the editor link and say that Publish is there. Publishing is public:
the guide appears under their nickname and search engines index it.

Publishing needs a public nickname, a title of 8-90 characters and at least one `media` block with
the user's own generation. A guide holds up to 60 blocks, 20 media items, 15 links and 20 000
characters of text; captions up to 300.

## Posting it

The user posts the result themselves. Make the media in the placement's ratio, keep the hook in the
first 125 characters of the caption, and pair a "comment WORD" call with the keyword the user's
auto-reply listens for.
